title: 8 in 10 Americans Take Health Supplements
paragraphs: Taking vitamins and other health supplements has become a normal part of daily life for most Americans, according to a new survey by the Pew Research Center.
The survey asked 3,554 adults in the United States about their health habits in July 2026. It found that 78%, or about eight in ten, currently take at least one supplement for their health.

Vitamins and minerals, such as iron, calcium and multivitamins, were by far the most common type of supplement. Around 67% of adults said they take them. In addition, 31% take protein supplements, 25% take omega oils, such as fish oil, and 19% take herbal supplements, such as ginseng. Around 35% take other types, such as melatonin or probiotics.

The survey revealed some clear differences between groups. Older adults were more likely to take supplements than younger adults. Around 85% of people aged 65 and older take them, compared with 67% of people aged 18 to 29. However, younger people were more likely to take protein supplements. Women were also more likely than men to take supplements, at 82% compared with 74%. People with higher incomes were more likely to take supplements than those with lower incomes.

Many people believe supplements are important for their health. For example, 62% of people who take vitamins or minerals said they were extremely or very important to their health. Protein supplements were the type that users were least likely to see as very important.

However, it is worth noting that supplements are not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for safety and effectiveness before they are sold, unlike medicines. Whether supplements actually benefit health has long been debated, and many medical professionals advise caution.
Meanwhile, the global supplement market was worth an estimated $209.5 billion in 2025.
